name: Matthew P Flake
current_role: CEO, President and Chairman of the Board, Q2 Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: QTWO), Austin, TX
profile: Matt Flake is the longtime CEO of Q2 Holdings, an Austin-based digital banking software provider for banks, credit unions and fintechs. He joined founder Hank Seale's startup as VP of sales in 2005, became president in 2008 and CEO in 2011, took it public in 2014, and succeeded Seale as chairman in June 2024. A Baylor graduate, he earlier sold at S1 Corp. and Q-UP Systems.
interesting_fact: He was Q2's first sales hire under founder Hank Seale (who founded Q2 in 2004) and has led the company from a ~75-person startup to a public digital-banking platform; he was named chairman in 2024 when Seale became chairman emeritus.
deep_cut_fact: He became Q2's president almost by accident: in 2008, with ~75 staff, he told Seale the company needed regular meetings, and Seale replied, "Screw that, you're president." He joined in 2005 as VP of sales: "I was the sales guy. But, it was the title that I wanted."
notes: Sources differ on when he became CEO (he says 2011, the Q2 Software subsidiary; some list Oct 2013 for the holding company). Best route is the Q2 media contact (Carly Baker).

name: Adam Joseph Lowe
current_role: Chief Product & Innovation Officer, CompoSecure, Inc. (NASDAQ: CMPO), Somerset, NJ; creator of the Arculus platform
profile: Dr. Adam Lowe is CompoSecure's Chief Product & Innovation Officer, leading R&D at the premium metal payment-card maker. After about six years in its R&D group he became the company's first Chief Innovation Officer in 2020, and he created Arculus, CompoSecure's crypto cold-storage wallet and passwordless authentication platform, launched in 2021.
interesting_fact: He named Arculus after the Roman god of safes and strongboxes. The product turns a metal card into a crypto cold-storage wallet and a tap-to-phone authenticator with three-factor protection.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech he worked in government defense-department labs. He holds a BS in Microbiology from Salisbury University and a PhD and MBA from Cornell, where his doctoral research was in bio-nanotechnology. He is listed as an inventor on 200+ patents and patents pending.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (Finovate, Consensus, Seamless, Singapore FinTech Festival), so a speaking or podcast invite is a natural angle. Patent counts in his bios range from a dozen to 500+, so don't quote a number.

name: Ryan Carver
current_role: Chief Development Officer, Soluna Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: SLNH), appointed July 2026; based in Seattle
profile: Ryan Carver joined Soluna, a developer of renewable-powered data centers for AI/HPC and bitcoin mining, as Chief Development Officer in July 2026. He leads development, construction, tech operations and power. He spent over a decade at Microsoft, most recently as Senior Director of AI Construction & Site Development, running a construction P&L in the tens of billions of dollars.
interesting_fact: At Microsoft he led the construction program for the Fairwater AI data center campus in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, one of the largest AI supercomputing sites in the world.
deep_cut_fact: Before data centers he was an engineer and project manager at Turner Construction and Jacobs, working on World Trade Center Tower 2 and Yankee Stadium. He has an International Business degree from Ohio State and is a Certified Construction Manager (CCM).

public_contacts.value: West of Fairfax for Soluna: Soluna@westof.co

notes: Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast: a hyperscale AI campus builder now at a renewable-energy data-center developer. His insider holdings are mostly new-hire equity, since he joined in July 2026. Go through Soluna's PR agency.

name: William N. Mathis
current_role: Managing Partner, Conti Street Partners LLC (Houston); former independent director of Black Stone Minerals (2015 to Oct 2025)
profile: Will Mathis is a Houston investor with long experience in oil and gas. He sat on the board of mineral-and-royalty owner Black Stone Minerals' general partner and chaired its Nominating and Governance Committee, resigning in October 2025. He has been managing member of Wellspring Energy Partners.
interesting_fact: Beyond energy he has been active in aquaculture: he chaired Australis Aquaculture from 2009, and his WM Capital (an affiliate of Conti Street Partners) later bought Australis's U.S. and Vietnamese barramundi-farming operations.
deep_cut_fact: A Davidson College graduate, he served on Davidson's board and executive committee. He has also served on the boards of the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, The Chinquapin School, The Brown Foundation, Texas Medical Center and Texas Children's Hospital.
notes: Low public profile and no personal website or social accounts found. He left the BSM board on Oct 30, 2025 'to focus on other commitments' (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251103042044/en). The barramundi venture is a good conversational hook.

name: James Grant Conroy
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Ross Stores, Inc. (NASDAQ: ROST), since Feb 2025; director, Sally Beauty Holdings
profile: Jim Conroy is CEO of off-price retailer Ross Stores. He joined as CEO-elect in Dec 2024 and succeeded Barbara Rentler in Feb 2025. From late 2012 he led Boot Barn, growing it from 86 stores in eight Western states to a national brand with roughly fivefold sales (~$1.7B) and taking it public in 2014. Before that he was president and COO of Claire's.
interesting_fact: When he took Boot Barn public in 2014 the shares priced at $16. By late 2024 they had risen more than tenfold to almost $170, and the stock fell 20% the day his move to Ross was announced.
deep_cut_fact: An early job was VP of strategic planning at Blockbuster (1996-98), which he called "an incredibly entrepreneurial company." He later ran buying, marketing and supply chain for the ~300-store Gerald Stevens Flowers & Gifts chain. He holds undergraduate and MBA degrees from Cornell.

public_contacts.value: connie.kao@ros.com (Connie Kao, SVP Investor & Media Relations)

notes: The Ross contact handles both investor and media relations. He is a retail operator, not an energy or data-center figure.

name: Bonnie K Wachtel
current_role: Principal and Director, Wachtel & Co., Inc. (Washington, DC); independent director, VSE Corporation (NASDAQ: VSEC) since 1991
profile: Bonnie Wachtel is a Washington, DC-based investment banker and longtime public-company director. She is principal of the boutique brokerage and investment bank Wachtel & Co. and has sat on the board of aviation aftermarket company VSE Corp since 1991. She has been a director of six Nasdaq-listed companies, including ExOne (2013-21).
interesting_fact: She has served on VSE Corporation's board for 35 years, since 1991. In that time VSE changed from a government services contractor into an aviation aftermarket parts and MRO company.
deep_cut_fact: From 2006 to 2016 she sat on Nasdaq's Listing Qualifications hearing panel, which rules on whether companies may stay listed. She is a CFA charterholder and a member of the District of Columbia Bar.
notes: Low media profile. The VSE IR email reaches the company, not her directly. Wachtel & Co. is her own firm, but its site publishes no email. Sources disagree on her education (University of Chicago MBA; UVA JD per some profiles).

name: Harrie Schippers
current_role: Retired. Former President (2018-2025) and CFO of PACCAR Inc (NASDAQ: PCAR); retired in 2025 after 39 years with the company
profile: Harrie Schippers is a Dutch truck-industry executive who spent 39 years at PACCAR, maker of Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF trucks. He was president of DAF Trucks in Eindhoven from 2010 to 2016, then became PACCAR CFO in Bellevue, WA, and President and CFO in 2018. He handed the CFO role to Brice Poplawski in June 2025, and Kevin Baney became president on Jan 1, 2026.
interesting_fact: While he led DAF, it developed the CF and XF truck ranges, which won International Truck of the Year 2018. PACCAR's CEO credited the trucks to his leadership when he was promoted.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an M.S. in Economics from Tilburg University. He is one of the few Dutch executives to rise from a European subsidiary (DAF, Eindhoven) to president of the U.S. parent PACCAR.
notes: Retired, per Trucking Dive (https://www.truckingdive.com/news/paccar-cfo-to-retire-harrie-schippers/745063/) and FleetOwner. Some aggregator sites still list him as president/CFO, but that is stale. No personal public channels found.

name: Lex Greensill
current_role: No current corporate role. Founder of Greensill Capital (collapsed March 2021); banned from serving as a UK company director for nine years in 2026
profile: Lex Greensill is an Australian-born financier who founded Greensill Capital in London in 2011 after stints at Morgan Stanley and Citigroup. The supply-chain-finance firm was valued at about $4B and backed by SoftBank, but it filed for insolvency in March 2021. He is no longer a billionaire and faces multiple lawsuits and regulatory action over the collapse.
interesting_fact: He was made a CBE in the 2017 Birthday Honours for services to business, and he had earlier worked as a senior adviser to UK Prime Minister David Cameron's government, with an office at 10 Downing Street.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Bundaberg, Queensland, and worked as a sugarcane farmer on the family's sugarcane and melon farm before going into banking. He moved to Britain in 2001.
notes: High reputational risk: Greensill Capital's 2021 collapse led to litigation, the Cameron lobbying scandal and a 2026 nine-year UK director disqualification. Not a fit for positive outreach. Found no public contact channels. Web search budget ran out, so this profile relies on Wikipedia.

name: Gregory Bailey
current_role: CEO, Juvenescence Limited (longevity biotech); director, Biohaven Ltd (NYSE: BHVN) and Serina Therapeutics (NYSE: SER); managing partner, MediqVentures
profile: Dr. Greg Bailey, 70, is a Canadian-trained physician turned biotech financier. He was the initial financier and an independent director of Medivation (2005-2012) and a long-time director of Biohaven. He now leads Juvenescence, a company developing therapies to extend healthy human lifespan. He chaired Portage Biotech until 2025.
interesting_fact: He was the initial financier of Medivation, the company behind the prostate-cancer drug Xtandi, which Pfizer bought in 2016 for about $14B. He also co-founded VirnetX, Ascent Healthcare Solutions and DuraMedic.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into finance he practised emergency medicine for ten years. He earned his MD at the University of Western Ontario.
notes: The Medivation $14B figure is general knowledge; the proxy only confirms that he was its initial financier and a director. Juvenescence (longevity) is the best angle. The search budget ran out, so I could not verify the Juvenescence press contact (juvenescence.com is now a parked domain).

name: Benny Landa
current_role: Chairman, The Landa Group / Landa Labs (Rehovot, Israel); founder of Landa Digital Printing
profile: Benny Landa, born 1946 in Poland and raised in Edmonton, Canada, is an Israeli inventor known as the 'father of commercial digital printing.' He founded Indigo in 1977, launched the E-Print 1000 digital color press in 1993 and sold Indigo to HP for $830M in 2002. He then started The Landa Group for nanotechnology, which produced Landa Digital Printing's 'Nanography' inkjet-to-belt presses.
interesting_fact: His Indigo idea came from his father, who in Edmonton built a camera from bicycle parts and pulleys that captured images directly onto photographic paper without film. Landa applied that 'filmless' concept to printing.
deep_cut_fact: His first job (1969) was at CAPS, a micrographics research firm. A product he helped develop won a major Rolls-Royce Aero Engine contract and made him head of R&D. In 2002 he and his wife set up the Landa Fund, which has given $50M+ in university scholarships in Israel.
notes: His Landa Group nanotech research has included capturing ambient heat to convert into electricity, a possible energy-podcast angle. Web search budget ran out, so I could not check Landa Digital Printing's latest corporate status (2024-26). Confirm before outreach.

name: Juan De Antonio
profile: Juan de Antonio Rubio is a Spanish telecom engineer with a Stanford MBA. In May 2011 he founded Cabify, a Madrid-based ride-hailing and mobility platform operating in Spain and Latin America, which became Spain's first unicorn. He still runs the company as CEO.
interesting_fact: Cabify began as 'Executive', a niche premium service with high-end cars priced slightly above taxis. The cheaper 'Cabify Lite', launched in 2013, made up 85% of its offer by the end of 2015.
deep_cut_fact: He started Cabify after an unsuccessful attempt to bring electric vehicles to European cities. He first talked the idea over with Tuenti co-founder Adeyemi Ajao and Brendan Wallace, who became advisors.
notes: Good energy angle: his original electric-vehicle ambition, and Cabify's later push to electrify its fleet. Web search budget ran out, so I did not verify his personal social accounts; confirm before use.

name: Ciaran Lee
current_role: Co-founder of Intercom (renamed Fin, AI customer-service platform); current role not verified
profile: Ciaran Lee is an Irish engineer and one of Intercom's four co-founders, with Eoghan McCabe, Des Traynor and David Barrett. The company was founded in California in 2011 and grew into a customer-messaging platform valued at over $1B. It has since rebranded as Fin, an AI-driven customer-service company headquartered in San Francisco.
interesting_fact: Intercom was funded by an earlier exit. The founders' Dublin design consultancy Contrast built the bug-tracking tool Exceptional, sold it to Rackspace in 2011, and used the proceeds to start Intercom. Twitter co-founder Biz Stone invested in 2012.
notes: Very low public profile. I could not confirm his current role or whether he is still at Fin/Intercom. An @ciaranlee X account exists but is empty and unverified, so it is not listed. Web search budget ran out before I could research him further.

name: Nicolas Jammet
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Concept Officer and director, Sweetgreen, Inc. (NYSE: SG), Los Angeles
profile: Nicolas Jammet co-founded salad chain Sweetgreen in 2006 with Georgetown classmates Jonathan Neman and Nathaniel Ru. It opened its first store in DC in 2007, three months after they graduated, grew to 250+ locations and listed on the NYSE in 2021. He was president (2009-14) and co-CEO (2014-17). As Chief Concept Officer since 2017 he oversees supply chain, automation and culinary.
interesting_fact: The founders started Sweetgreen because they were disappointed with campus food at Georgetown. They raised their first $375,000 from backers including restaurateur Joe Bastianich and Honest Tea co-founder Seth Goldman.
deep_cut_fact: His remit now covers Sweetgreen's automation push, built on its 2021 acquisition of Boston robotic-kitchen startup Spyce. He has sat on Sweetgreen's board since October 2009 and was its corporate Secretary from 2020 to Feb 2026.
notes: Age 41 per the 2026 proxy. The kitchen-automation (robotics) angle fits an entrepreneurship podcast. I did not verify his personal social accounts because the search budget ran out.

name: Milda Mitkute
current_role: Co-founder of Vinted (Vilnius, Lithuania); current role not verified
profile: Milda Mitkutė co-founded Vinted with Justas Janauskas in Vilnius in 2008. It began as a Lithuanian site for swapping clothes and became Europe's largest second-hand fashion marketplace, with €10.8bn GMV and €1.1bn revenue in 2025 across 26+ markets. Thomas Plantenga has run the company as CEO since the late 2010s.
interesting_fact: Vinted began when Mitkutė was moving house and wanted a way to get rid of clothes she no longer needed. Janauskas helped her build a website where people could trade clothing.
deep_cut_fact: The company's original name was Mano Drabužiai, Lithuanian for 'my clothing', before it became Vinted.
notes: Low public profile, with no English or Lithuanian Wikipedia page. I could not verify her current activities or whether she still holds a Vinted role. The search budget ran out, so check again before outreach.

name: Xia Dingding
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of Xinchao, a Chinese media company valued at about $1B. Xinchao Media (新潮传媒, Chengdu elevator-screen advertising) is generally associated with founder Zhang Jixue, so I could not confirm that this name matches that company or its founding team.
notes: Identity unresolved. The name may be a transliteration error, or may refer to a co-founder of a different 'Xinchao'. The web search budget ran out and Chinese sources (Baidu Baike, zh-Wikipedia) were unreachable, so manual checking is needed before any use.

name: Frederik Pfisterer
current_role: Co-founder of Mambu (cloud core-banking SaaS, Amsterdam/Berlin); current role not verified
profile: Frederik Pfisterer co-founded Mambu in Berlin in 2011 with Eugene Danilkis and Sofia Nunes and led its technology. The cloud core-banking platform began by serving microfinance lenders, grew to $165M contracted ARR by 2022, and was valued at $5.3B in December 2021 after a €200M EQT-led round. Fernando Zandona has been CEO since 2023.
interesting_fact: Mambu was one of Germany's highest-valued fintech unicorns, at $5.3B in Dec 2021. It began with early funding from Commerzbank and the VC firm Point Nine.
deep_cut_fact: Mambu started as a one-year capstone project by five students in Carnegie Mellon's Master of Human-Computer Interaction program. It included field research with microfinance institutions in Mozambique, and three of the team then founded the company.
notes: Low public profile, and his current role at Mambu is unclear. The web search budget ran out before I could check his own channels or a Mambu press email (the newsroom page shows no email).

name: Mate Pencz
current_role: Co-founder of Loft (São Paulo proptech / real-estate platform); current title not verified
profile: Mate Pencz co-founded Loft, a Brazilian real-estate technology platform for buying, selling and renting homes that Hurun lists at about a $2B valuation. Loft now also sells software and rental-guarantee products to real-estate agencies in São Paulo, Rio, Belo Horizonte, Porto Alegre and other Brazilian cities.
notes: Web search budget ran out and Wikipedia has no page on him or Loft, so the biography is minimal and unverified. I believe he is a serial founder in Brazil (with co-founder Florian Hagenbuch) but did not confirm it, so it is left out of the facts. Research further before outreach.

name: Erik Svenson
current_role: Co-founder of Blockstream (Bitcoin infrastructure, Menlo Park/Victoria BC); current title not verified
profile: Erik Svenson is a co-founder of Blockstream, the Bitcoin infrastructure company started in 2014 with Adam Back, Pieter Wuille and others, according to Blockstream's own history page. Blockstream raised a $21M seed round in 2014 and reached a $3.2B valuation in a $210M Series B in 2021. It builds sidechains (Liquid), Lightning software, hardware wallets and Bitcoin mining operations.
interesting_fact: Blockstream launched Blockstream Satellite in 2017 to broadcast the Bitcoin blockchain from space, so nodes can sync without internet access. It also runs Bitcoin mining operations, which is relevant to an energy and data-center podcast.
notes: Low public profile, and Wikipedia's founder list for Blockstream omits him, though Blockstream's site names him. I could not verify his current role (reportedly an early president/executive) because the search budget ran out. Blockstream's planned SPAC listing with Cantor was cancelled in July 2026.

name: Charles Cascarilla
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, Paxos (Paxos Trust Company), New York
profile: Charles Cascarilla co-founded Paxos with Rich Teo in 2012 as the itBit bitcoin exchange. It became a regulated blockchain-infrastructure company and stablecoin issuer, behind Pax Dollar (USDP), PayPal USD (PYUSD) and Global Dollar (USDG). Paxos has raised $500M+ (Oak HC/FT, Founders Fund, PayPal Ventures) at a $2.4B valuation.
interesting_fact: In 2015 Paxos (then itBit) won a New York DFS limited-purpose trust charter, making it one of the first U.S. companies approved and regulated to offer crypto products. In 2018 it launched Paxos Standard, one of the first regulated stablecoins.
notes: A prominent stablecoin/fintech CEO and frequent speaker. No press email appears in static HTML on paxos.com/newsroom, so check the newsroom for a media contact. Web search budget ran out before a deep-cut fact could be sourced.

name: Josefin Landgård
current_role: Founder and CEO, MANTLE (Swedish skincare brand), since 2019; co-founder of Kry/Livi
profile: Josefin Landgård, born 1983, is a Swedish entrepreneur who co-founded the digital healthcare company Kry (Livi in the UK and France) and was its acting CEO from 2014 to 2018. It grew into one of Europe's largest telehealth providers, with Hurun valuing it at about $2B. She earlier founded and ran Glossybox in Sweden. Since 2019 she has led the clean-clinical skincare brand MANTLE.
interesting_fact: She named MANTLE after the skin's 'acid mantle', the top layer of the skin barrier. The brand's biomimetic formulas are developed in its own Swedish laboratory.
deep_cut_fact: She grew up in Leksand and went to a ski-focused upper-secondary school in Malung. While studying at the Stockholm School of Economics she coached for the Saltsjöbaden slalom club, and she was later COO of the ski maker Faction Skis.
notes: Best route is through MANTLE, her current company. Kry's press office would be the alternative for a telehealth angle. I did not verify her social accounts because the search budget ran out.
